answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a deposit for 30 days and allocates job access in proportion to deposited stake. Whether an agent is named zephyr, plume, or meadow, its name earns no extra access. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities gives the same total allocation as staking them under one identity. To gain more access, an attacker must lock more capital, sacrificing its use elsewhere for the full term.
